presentingComplaint: Cough productive of blood-streaked sputum for 6 weeks with drenching night sweats and 8 kg weight loss, on a background of TB treatment 2 years ago said to be 'incomplete'.
history: Auto-rickshaw driver from an urban resettlement colony in Delhi. Cough began ~6 weeks ago, initially dry then productive of mucopurulent, occasionally blood-streaked sputum. Reports evening-predominant low-grade fever, soaking night sweats, anorexia and unintentional weight loss of about 8 kg over 2 months. Was diagnosed with smear-positive pulmonary TB two years ago and took the government DOTS regimen but self-discontinued after roughly 3 months once he felt better; no documented cure. Wife completed a full course of TB treatment last year. Non-smoker of beedis for 20 years, occasional alcohol. No HIV risk factors elicited but status unknown. No prior hospitalisation this episode. This presentation is a treatment-after-loss-to-follow-up relapse and the resistance question is central.
examination: Thin, chronically ill-appearing man (BMI 17). No respiratory distress at rest. Oral thrush absent. Right upper zone bronchial breathing with post-tussive crepitations and a few coarse crackles; no pleural rub. No lymphadenopathy, no clubbing. Cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable, no hepatosplenomegaly. No focal neurology.
imaging: Chest radiograph: right upper lobe fibrocavitary disease with a thick-walled cavity, surrounding nodular infiltrates and volume loss with tracheal deviation to the right; no pleural effusion. Findings consistent with reactivation/relapse cavitary TB.
microbiology: Sputum for AFB smear: 3+ acid-fast bacilli. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra: MTB detected, HIGH bacillary load, rifampicin resistance DETECTED. Reflex line-probe assay (first- and second-line): rpoB mutation confirming rifampicin resistance, katG mutation (high-level isoniazid resistance); fluoroquinolone (gyrA/gyrB) and amikacin/capreomycin loci wild-type — i.e., RR/MDR-TB without detected fluoroquinolone resistance. Liquid (MGIT) culture and phenotypic DST sent. Baseline audiometry, ECG (QTc) and visual acuity documented before starting second-line therapy.
differentialDiagnoses: Multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis (rifampicin + isoniazid resistant) — confirmed
Post-primary reactivation drug-susceptible TB (excluded by Xpert rifampicin resistance)
Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis / aspergilloma colonising an old cavity
Lung abscess or bronchiectasis with secondary infection
finalDiagnosis: Multidrug-resistant (rifampicin- and isoniazid-resistant) cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis — relapse after loss to follow-up, fluoroquinolone-susceptible
citations: WHO — Consolidated Guidelines on Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Treatment (BPaLM/BPaL regimen) — 2022
India NTEP / Central TB Division — Programmatic Management of Drug-Resistant TB (PMDT) Guidelines — 2021
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Tuberculosis (drug-resistant TB)
stewardship: This is antimicrobial stewardship applied to TB: rifampicin resistance on Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra mandates escalation OFF the standard first-line regimen (continuing isoniazid/rifampicin would amplify resistance). Empiric first-line 4-drug therapy is NOT acceptable here. With confirmed RR/MDR-TB and NO detected fluoroquinolone resistance, the WHO 2022-preferred pathway is the all-oral 6-month BPaLM regimen — bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid and moxifloxacin. Baseline QTc, LFTs, visual acuity, FBC and audiometry are checked; ECG and haemoglobin/ANC are monitored for QT prolongation (bedaquiline + moxifloxacin) and linezolid myelotoxicity/optic neuritis. 'Source control' in TB terms = achieving smear/culture conversion plus airborne-isolation and public-health notification: notify under NTEP, start DOT/adherence support, screen household contacts, and re-establish the follow-up that previously failed. Phenotypic DST is awaited to confirm the regimen and de-escalate/adjust (e.g., drop or extend based on fluoroquinolone and linezolid tolerance).
contraindications: Do NOT continue standard first-line HRZE once rifampicin resistance is confirmed — risks amplifying resistance
Bedaquiline + moxifloxacin: additive QT prolongation — avoid/monitor with other QT-prolonging drugs and correct K+/Mg2+
Linezolid: cumulative dose-related myelosuppression, peripheral and optic neuropathy — monitor FBC and vision, dose-reduce if toxicity
Avoid empiric fluoroquinolone monotherapy for the 'chest infection' before TB is excluded — masks disease and selects fluoroquinolone-resistant TB
edgeCases: If reflex testing had shown gyrA/gyrB fluoroquinolone resistance (pre-XDR), moxifloxacin would be dropped and a BPaL-based / individualised longer regimen used
HIV co-infection would mandate ART timing coordination and drug-interaction review (bedaquiline levels)
QTc >500 ms or profound cytopenia during therapy requires interruption/substitution rather than dose continuation
expectedMaiK: Rifampicin resistance on Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra in relapsed cavitary TB defines RR/MDR-TB and requires escalation to a WHO-recommended all-oral second-line regimen (BPaLM), not first-line HRZE.
